enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 201–210 regulate termination of agency by revocation, renunciation, completion, death or insanity, protect an agent’s interest in the subject matter in section 202, prescribe limits on revocation after partial exercise, notice requirements and the effect of termination on agents and third persons.

Definition: Termination of agency determines when the agent’s authority ends and when the principal, agent and third persons cease to be bound by the agency.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the basis of termination.
2. Check whether the agent has an interest protected by section 202.
3. If revocation or renunciation occurs, apply the compensation and notice rules.
4. Determine when termination becomes effective against the agent and third persons.
5. Apply the post-termination duties concerning principal’s death or insanity.
examples: A appoints B as agent with an interest in the subject matter of the agency; section 202 limits the principal’s ordinary power to revoke the authority to the prejudice of that interest.
problemApplication: Apply sections 201–210: identify the agency relationship and statutory mechanism, test each condition, consider the opposing argument, and conclude.
keyTakeaways: Sections 201–210 regulate termination of agency by revocation, renunciation, completion, death or insanity, protect an agent’s interest in the subject matter in section 202, prescribe limits on revocation after partial exercise, notice requirements and the effect of termination on agents and third persons.
Termination of agency determines when the agent’s authority ends and when the principal, agent and third persons cease to be bound by the agency.
